mainTopic: Who may order a document and who pays the סופר, and how a סופר makes sure he knows the names on a גט or שובר
overview: The משנה lists kinds of documents and says whose request is enough for a סופר to write each one, and who pays him. A loan שטר may be written at the לוה's request alone, and a bill of sale at the מוכר's request alone. Documents of אירוסין and נשואין, farming contracts, and court records need both sides to agree. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that each side gets his own copy of a court record. The גמרא then goes back to the earlier rule that a סופר may write a גט or a שובר only if he 'recognizes' the people. רב explains this as knowing their names, and אביי says both spouses' names must be known. The sages raise more worries about people with the same name or a false name. רב's rules answer them: two men with the same name in one city divorce only in each other's presence, and a name known in the city for thirty days is trusted. The amud ends with a story about רב ירמיה בר אבא and a disputed receipt, and אביי begins a new statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A loan document: the borrower may order it alone, and he pays
steps.stepSummary: A סופר may write a loan שטר at the לוה's request even if the מלוה is not there. He may not write it at the מלוה's request unless the לוה is there. The לוה pays the fee.
steps.simpleTranslation: A scribe may write a loan document for the borrower even if the lender is not with him. He may not write one for the lender unless the borrower is with him. The borrower pays the scribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the loan document and tells us whose request is enough to have it written, and who pays the סופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan שטר obligates the לוה, so when he asks for it himself, he is only taking on a debt against himself. If the מלוה could order one alone, he could make a document for a debt that may not exist, so the לוה must be present. The לוה pays, because he is the one who needs the document to get the loan.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal document, here a loan document

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up לֹוֶה (borrower) with מַלְוֶה (lender). The words look almost the same, but the rule is the opposite for each one.

phrases.english: We write a document for the borrower

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מַלְוֶה עִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: even though the lender is not with him,
but we do not write for the lender
unless the borrower is with him.
And the borrower pays the fee.
phrases.notes: The fee here is the scribe's pay for writing the document.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָר לַלֹּוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening ruling of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan שטר may be written at the לוה's request alone, but not at the מלוה's request alone. The לוה pays the סופר.

steps.title: A sale document: the seller may order it alone, and the buyer pays
steps.stepSummary: A סופר may write a bill of sale at the מוכר's request even if the לוקח is not there. He may not write it at the לוקח's request unless the מוכר is there. The לוקח pays the fee.
steps.simpleTranslation: A scribe may write a bill of sale for the seller even if the buyer is not with him. He may not write one for the buyer unless the seller is with him. The buyer pays the scribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same pattern to a sale document. The side giving something up may order it alone, and the side who gains pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the מוכר is the one giving up his field, so he plays the same role as the לוה in step 1. But the fee now goes to the other side: the לוקח pays, because the bill of sale protects his purchase. So the payer is not always the one who may order the document alone. The payer is whoever benefits from it.
steps.confusionAlert: In the loan case, the same person who may order the document (the לוה) also pays. In the sale case, the one who may order it (the מוכר) does NOT pay. The לוקח does.

phrases.english: We write a document for the seller

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לוֹקֵחַ עִמּוֹ,
phrases.english: even though the buyer is not with him,
but we do not write for the buyer
unless the seller is with him.
And the buyer pays the fee.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָר לַמּוֹכֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same who-may-order rule to sales, but the fee goes the other way
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bill of sale may be written at the מוכר's request alone, but not at the לוקח's request alone. The לוקח pays the סופר.

steps.title: Betrothal and marriage documents need both sides, and the groom pays
steps.stepSummary: Documents of אירוסין and נשואין are written only with the agreement of both sides. The חתן pays the fee.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not write betrothal and marriage documents unless both sides agree. The groom pays the scribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a different kind of document. For betrothal and marriage papers, neither side may order them alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike a loan or a sale, these documents set obligations on both sides. So no single side can order them alone, and both must agree. The חתן pays the fee.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
With the agreement of both of them

phrases.english: We do not write documents of betrothal and marriage
except with the agreement of both of them,
phrases.notes: "Both of them" means the groom and the bride.

phrases.english: and the groom pays the fee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָרֵי אֵירוּסִין וְנִשּׂוּאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from one-sided documents to documents needing both sides
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Documents of אירוסין and נשואין need the agreement of both sides. The חתן pays the סופר.

steps.title: Farming contracts need both sides, and the tenant pays
steps.stepSummary: Contracts of אריסות and קבלנות are written only with the agreement of both sides. The מקבל, who receives the field to work, pays the fee.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not write sharecropping or tenancy contracts unless both sides agree. The one who receives the field pays the scribe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list with farming contracts. Like marriage documents, they need both sides to agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In these contracts, the field owner and the worker each take on duties, so both must agree before the document is written. The מקבל pays, because he is the one who wants the contract that secures his right to work the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Sharecropping: working someone's field for a share of the crop
Contracting: taking a field for a fixed payment
The one who receives the field to work it

steps.whatToRemember: Two questions run through the whole משנה. (1) Whose request is enough? For loans and sales, the side taking on the obligation may order the document alone. For marriage and farming contracts, both sides must agree. (2) Who pays? Always the side who benefits from the document: the לוה, the לוקח, the חתן, and the מקבל.

phrases.english: We do not write a contract of sharecropping and contracting
except with the agreement of both of them,
phrases.notes: Here "both" means the field owner and the worker.

phrases.english: and the one who receives the field pays the fee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטַר אֲרִיסוּת וְקַבְּלָנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 3, applying the both-sides rule to farming contracts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Contracts of אריסות and קבלנות need the agreement of both sides. The מקבל pays the סופר.

steps.title: Arbitration and court documents need both sides, and both pay
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that שטרי בירורין and all court records are written only when both sides agree, and both sides pay the סופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A סופר does not write arbitration documents or any other court record unless both sides agree. Both sides pay him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more case in its list of documents. This time the document belongs equally to both sides, so both must agree and both must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases, one side gained from the document, so that side paid. Here neither side gains more than the other, because the record serves both. That is why the משנה requires both to agree and both to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Documents recording which judges each side chose for arbitration
Any official court record or decision
With the agreement of both sides

phrases.english: One does not write documents of arbitration
phrases.notes: In arbitration, each side picks a judge, and this document records those picks.

phrases.english: or any court record
except with the agreement of both of them,
and both of them pay the fee.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָרֵי בֵּירוּרִין וְכׇל מַעֲשֵׂה בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of documents. This one belongs to both sides equally, so both pay.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Court documents and arbitration records need the agreement of both sides, and both share the fee.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: write a separate copy for each side
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the סופר writes two copies, one for each side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: for the two sides, the סופר writes two documents, one for this person and one for that person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds to the ruling about court documents. Each side should get his own copy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the document serves both sides, each one may need to show it later. A single copy would leave one side without proof, so each side gets his own.

keyTerms.meaning: One for this person by himself

steps.whatToRemember: Loan documents and bills of sale: the side who gains pays. Documents of marriage and field contracts: both must agree, and one named side pays. Court documents: both must agree, and both pay. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that each side gets his own copy.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
for the two of them, one writes two documents,
one for this one by himself, and one for that one by himself.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: תוספת (an added point within the משנה)
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לִשְׁנֵיהֶם כּוֹתְבִין שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second opinion about how court documents are written.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two copies are written, one for each side.

steps.title: What does 'provided that he recognizes them' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins by asking what the משנה meant by the condition 'provided that he recognizes them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'provided that he recognizes them' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking about a line from earlier in the משנה. This question sets up רב's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the משנה allowed a סופר to write a גט for a husband even if the wife is not there. It also allowed him to write a שובר for a wife even if the husband is not there. But it added that he must 'recognize them,' and the גמרא wants to know exactly whom he must recognize.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not in the part of the משנה quoted just above. It comes from the earlier part about a גט and a שובר.

phrases.english: גמרא: What is meant by
'provided that he recognizes them'?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה's rule about writing a גט or a שובר when only one spouse is present.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא מַכִּירָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא leaves the end of the משנה and goes back to explain an earlier condition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whom must the סופר recognize, and what must he recognize about them?

steps.title: רב: the man's name for a גט, the woman's name for a שובר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: the סופר must know the man's name when writing a גט, and the woman's name when writing a שובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it means he must recognize the man's name in a גט, and the woman's name in a שובר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The סופר must know the name of the person who asks for the document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband asks for the גט, so the סופר must be sure the man is really who he says he is. The wife asks for the שובר, so the סופר must be sure of her identity. רב mentions only the name of the person making the request.

keyTerms.meaning: A receipt; here, the wife confirms she was paid her כתובה

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
provided that he recognizes
the man's name in a bill of divorce,
and the woman's name in a receipt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא מַכִּיר שֵׁם הָאִישׁ בַּגֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The סופר must recognize the man's name for a גט and the woman's name for a שובר.

steps.title: The sages wonder: only one name in each case?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא, רב אחא בר הונא and רב הונא בר חיננא sat with אביי and asked whether רב really meant that only one name must be known.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא, רב אחא בר הונא and רב הונא בר חיננא were sitting, and אביי was sitting with them. As they sat, they asked: for a גט, the man's name must be known, but not the woman's? For a שובר, the woman's name must be known, but not the man's?
steps.whatsHappening: A group of sages questions how far רב's statement goes. They ask whether only one name really needs to be known, and this sets up their challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's wording seems to say the סופר needs to know only the person making the request. The sages find this surprising, because knowing just one side might not be enough. The next line shows the problem they see.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב סָפְרָא וְרַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Safra and Rav Acha bar Huna were sitting
with Rav Huna bar Chinnana,
and Abaye was sitting near them,
and as they sat, they asked:
The man's name in a bill of divorce, yes,
but the woman's name, no?!
The woman's name in a receipt, yes,
but the man's name, no?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיָתְבִי וְקָמִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רב's answer in step 8 is really limited to one name.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רב really mean that the other spouse's name does not need to be known?

steps.title: The danger: a גט given to another man's wife
steps.stepSummary: The sages state the problem. If the סופר does not know the wife, a man could take the גט and give it to someone else's wife who has the same name.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we should be worried: maybe he writes the גט, then goes and brings it to another man's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual challenge to רב. Knowing only the husband is not safe enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the סופר knows only the man who asks. That man could share a name with another woman's husband, and he could use the גט to falsely divorce her. So it seems the סופר should have to know both names, not just one.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of that other man

steps.whyThisMatters: A גט given to the wrong woman could make a married woman wrongly think she is divorced. That is why the sages take this worry so seriously.

phrases.english: But let us worry that maybe he writes a bill of divorce,
and goes and brings it
to the wife of that other man!
phrases.notes: He means another man with the same name as the one asking for the גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא כָּתֵב גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the sages questioned the one-name reading in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that only the man's name must be known for a גט
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the wife's identity is not checked, a man with the same name as her husband could use the גט to divorce another man's wife. So both names should need to be known.

steps.title: The same problem with the receipt
steps.stepSummary: The sages finish their challenge. If the סופר knows only the woman's name for a שובר, a woman could give the receipt to a man who is not her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And sometimes a woman will go, write a receipt, and give it to a man who is not her husband!
steps.whatsHappening: The sages are finishing the question they started in Step 10. They show that the same danger exists for the שובר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 the danger was a man misusing a גט. Here it is the mirror case. If the סופר knows only the woman's name, she could write a שובר saying she received her כתובה money and hand it to a different man whose wife has her name. That man could then use it to avoid paying his own wife.

keyTerms.meaning: who is not hers (not her husband)
a receipt; here, the wife's receipt that she was paid her כתובה

phrases.english: And sometimes a woman will go and write a receipt,
and give it to a man who is not her own [husband]!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזִמְנִין אָזְלָא כָּתְבָה אִשָּׁה שׁוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from Step 10 by applying it to the שובר
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that only the woman's name must be known for a שובר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Knowing only one name leaves the door open for fraud with a person who has the same name.

steps.title: אביי: both names must be known
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רב meant the סופר must know both the man and the woman for a גט, and also for a שובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: This is what רב meant. The man's name for a bill of divorce, and the same goes for the woman's name. The woman's name for a receipt, and the same goes for the man's name.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by reading רב's words differently. רב never meant that only one name is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב named only the main person in each document: the man who gives the גט, and the woman who gives the שובר. But 'the same applies' means the other spouse must be known too. Once the סופר knows both people, the fraud the sages described cannot happen.

phrases.english: Abaye said to them,
this is what Rav said:
The man's name for a bill of divorce [must be known],
and the same applies to the woman's name.
The woman's name for a receipt [must be known],
and the same applies to the man's name.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי, הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 10-11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the statement: רב's words are read more broadly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב required the סופר to know only one name in each document.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סופר must know both the man and the woman for both the גט and the שובר.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the סופר must know both spouses before writing either a גט or a שובר.

steps.title: What about two men with the same name?
steps.stepSummary: The sages challenge again. Even if the סופר knows both names, two men named יוסף בן שמעון might live in the same city, and one could use the גט for the other's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry about two men named יוסף בן שמעון who live in one city. Perhaps one will have a bill of divorce written, then go and bring it to the other man's wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The sages raise a new worry that still remains even after אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the names does not help if two couples share the very same names. The סופר knows 'יוסף בן שמעון' and his wife's name, but the גט fits both couples. So one man could misuse it to 'divorce' the other man's wife.

phrases.english: But let us be concerned about two men named Yosef ben Shimon
who live in one city,
perhaps one will have a bill of divorce written,
and go and bring it to the other man's wife!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵיחוּשׁ לִשְׁנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן הַדָּרִים בְּעִיר אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer: knowing both names is not enough when the names are shared
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that knowing both names prevents fraud
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Identical names for two couples make the names useless for telling them apart.

steps.title: Two men with the same name divorce only in each other's presence
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא answers with another rule from רב: two men named יוסף בן שמעון in one city may divorce their wives only when the other one is present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר הונא said to them: This is what רב said: Two men named יוסף בן שמעון who live in one city may divorce their wives only in each other's presence.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא answers the worry by quoting a separate rule of רב that already deals with this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a shared name lets one man misuse the גט for the other's wife. רב solved this by requiring each man to divorce only with the other one present. The other man can then make sure his own wife is not the one being divorced.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Aha bar Huna said to them,
this is what Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי יוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן הַדָּרִים בְּעִיר אַחַת –
phrases.english: Two men named Yosef ben Shimon who live in one city
may not divorce their wives
except in each other's presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא, הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing an existing rule that prevents the problem
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two men with the same name in one city leave room for misusing a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such men may divorce only in each other's presence, so no mistake can happen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a practical safeguard in the laws of גיטין for when names alone cannot tell people apart.

steps.title: What if a man falsely takes on the name in another city?
steps.stepSummary: The sages raise a further worry. A man could go to another city, establish himself there as יוסף בן שמעון, have a גט written, and use it for the real יוסף בן שמעון's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us worry that perhaps someone will go to another town and establish his name there as יוסף בן שמעון, have a bill of divorce written, and bring it to the other man's wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The sages raise another worry that the rules so far do not solve. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of 'in each other's presence' works only when both men are known in the same city. Here a stranger goes to a city where no one knows him and claims a false name. The סופר there thinks he 'knows' יוסף בן שמעון, but the man is lying, and the real man is not present.

keyTerms.meaning: he establishes his name (gets known by that name)

phrases.english: But let us be concerned that perhaps he will go to another town

phrases.aramaic: וּמַחְזֵיק לֵיהּ לִשְׁמֵיהּ בְּיוֹסֵף בֶּן שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: and get himself known by the name Yosef ben Shimon,
and have a bill of divorce written
and bring it to the other man's wife!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵיחוּשׁ דִּלְמָא אָזֵיל לְמָתָא אַחְרִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new case that the answers in Steps 12 and 14 do not cover
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that knowing the names (and the 'in each other's presence' rule) prevents fraud
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A man can fake a name in a place where no one knows him, so the סופר's 'knowing' the name does not protect the real husband's wife.

steps.title: A name known in the city for thirty days can be trusted
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא answers the worry from step 15 with a rule from רב: if a man's name has been known in the city for thirty days, we do not suspect it is false.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא told them that רב said: anyone whose name has been known in the city for thirty days, we do not worry about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the last worry, that a man could move to a new city and pretend to be יוסף בן שמעון. The answer is that once a name has been known in a city for thirty days, we trust it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was about a stranger who arrives and makes up a name. רב's rule sets a time limit: once he has been known by that name in the city for thirty days, we no longer suspect that the name is false.

keyTerms.meaning: Was established, became known as a settled fact
We are not concerned, we do not suspect

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule a סופר can rely on to write a גט for someone whose name he knows.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Ḥinnana said to them,
this is what Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהוּחְזַק שְׁמוֹ בָּעִיר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם –
phrases.english: anyone whose name has been established in the city for thirty days –
we are not concerned about him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא, הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry in step 15 about a man setting himself up under a false name in another city.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New rule from רב that limits the worry to people who have lived under the name for less than thirty days
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone could come to a new city, claim a name, and get a גט written right away.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once a name has been known in a city for thirty days, we trust it.

steps.title: What if the name is not yet known for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the rule is for a man whose name has not yet been known in the city for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his name was not yet established, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about a newcomer. This sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's rule only covers someone known for thirty days. The question is whether a newcomer can have a גט written before then, or whether there is some other way to confirm his name.

phrases.english: If it was not established, what is the rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא אִיתַּחְזַק, מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the case left open by רב's thirty-day rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How we treat a man whose name has been known in the city for less than thirty days.

steps.title: People call him by the name and he answers
steps.stepSummary: אביי says it is enough that people call him by that name and he responds.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is enough that they call him by the name and he answers.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. Even before thirty days, if people call him by this name and he answers, we can trust it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treats answering to a name as good enough evidence. A person who answers naturally when called is assumed to really have that name.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
that they call him by the name and he answers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ וְעָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Answering to the name when called is enough to trust it.

steps.title: A liar is careful to keep up his lie
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד disagrees: a liar is careful about his lies, so answering to a name proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: a liar is careful with his lying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד rejects אביי's test. A person who is lying about his name will make sure to answer when called by it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weakness in אביי's test is that a faker knows to answer to his fake name. So, according to רב זביד, answering does not prove anything, and a newcomer must wait the full thirty days.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
a liar – is careful about his lies.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד אָמַר: רַמָּאָה בְּרַמָּאוּתֵיהּ זְהִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אביי's answer in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's claim that answering to a name is enough proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A liar will deliberately answer to his false name, so answering proves nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: A name known in the city for thirty days is trusted. Before that, אביי says answering to the name is enough, while רב זביד says it is not, because a liar keeps up his lie.

steps.title: A woman denies she received the money on a receipt
steps.stepSummary: A story: רב ירמיה בר אבא signed as a witness on a receipt. A woman came and told him she was not the woman who had received the payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a receipt that רב ירמיה בר אבא signed as a witness. A certain woman came before him and said to him: It was not me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a שובר, a receipt saying a woman was paid her כתובה. The woman with that name claims she was not the one who got paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects to the earlier worry about two people with the same name. The woman says a different woman with her name gave that receipt, so she herself was never paid and still deserves her כתובה money.

phrases.english: There was a certain receipt

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה חֲתִים עֲלַהּ רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא.
phrases.english: on which Rav Yirmeya bar Abba was signed.
That woman came before him,
she said to him: It was not I.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא תְּבָרָא דַּהֲוָה חֲתִים עֲלַהּ רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rules about names to a real case of a receipt and a woman with the same name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman claims the receipt with her name belonged to a different woman.

steps.title: רב ירמיה explains why the other witnesses disagreed
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה says he also thought it was a different woman, but the other witnesses said she had just aged and her voice had changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I also told them it is not her, but they told me: she has grown old and her voice has become deeper.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה answers the woman. He had the same doubt at the time, but the other witnesses insisted it was really her and that she just looked and sounded older.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ירמיה did not recognize her face or voice, so he suspected a different woman. The other witnesses explained the difference by her aging, and they signed it as her receipt.

phrases.english: He said: I too said to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the other witnesses who signed the receipt with him.

phrases.english: It is not she,
and they said to me:
she has grown old –
and her voice has matured.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר, אֲנָא נָמֵי אֲמַרִי לְהוּ: לָאו אִיהִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב ירמיה's reply to the woman's claim in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He had doubted it too, but the other witnesses said it was the same woman, only older and with a changed voice.

steps.title: אביי begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: אביי opens a statement: even though the Sages said something, a point will follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: even though the Sages said:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a new statement. This line is only the setup, and the rest of his words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "even though" tell us אביי will quote a rule of the Sages and then add a limit or exception to it. We have to wait for the next part to see what he means.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: Abaye said: Even though the Sages said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אַף עַל גַּב דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story, אביי begins a new rule. It continues on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. אביי's actual rule continues on the next amud.
